tells.1: Generic template structure (capability claim, stat, 'could we help', 15-minute ask) with no detail specific to the prospect
tells.2: The opening 'Fairview is a regional grocery chain, and refrigerated freight is what we do' is a stiff relevance bridge that tells the prospect what their own company is
tells.3: Choppy one-sentence paragraphs and polished filler phrasing ('finished last year with a 99.2% on-time rate', 'discuss where we might fit') that read like a stock template

reason: Version 2 has concrete, checkable details: a named reference, remote temperature monitoring, and an honest definition of 'on time.' These build credibility and read like a real salesperson. Versions 1 and 3 are clean but interchangeable boilerplate.
